nodes.name: Western wheatgrass
nodes.desc: A cool-season native grass of the mixed-grass prairie. Prairie dogs and bison both feed on it in spring and early summer.

nodes.name: Blue grama
nodes.desc: A short, drought-tolerant prairie grass that grazers such as prairie dogs and bison eat.

nodes.name: Big sagebrush
nodes.desc: A grey-green shrub of the dry uplands. Prairie dogs eat shrubs like sagebrush in winter, and bison turn to it when grass is scarce.

nodes.name: Plains prickly pear
nodes.desc: A low cactus of the open prairie. Prairie dogs rely on it for food and moisture in winter.

nodes.name: American bison
nodes.desc: Reintroduced to the park. Mostly eats grasses and sedges, and its wallows are a form of ecosystem engineering that adds to prairie diversity.

nodes.name: Wild horse
nodes.desc: Free-roaming horses live in the South Unit. Park staff manage the herd size, and a fence keeps horses and bison inside the park.

nodes.name: Elk
nodes.desc: Reintroduced to the park. A large grazing and browsing deer that is managed by park staff along with bison and horses.

nodes.name: Black-tailed prairie dog
nodes.desc: Eats mostly grasses, plus prickly pear and shrubs in winter. Its burrowing mixes the soil and its colonies support many other species.

nodes.name: Pronghorn
nodes.desc: A fast prairie grazer and browser of open country, recorded often in the park area.

nodes.name: Mule deer
nodes.desc: A browsing deer of the draws and breaks, common in the badlands.

nodes.name: Migratory Grasshopper
nodes.desc: One of several grasshopper species recorded in the park area. It feeds on prairie grasses and forbs.

nodes.name: American badger
nodes.desc: A digging predator of burrowing rodents such as prairie dogs and pocket gophers.

nodes.name: Prairie rattlesnake
nodes.desc: A venomous snake that preys on small mammals, including prairie dogs, and shelters in burrows.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: A soaring scavenger that cleans up carcasses of animals such as deer and bison.

nodes.name: Black-billed Magpie
nodes.desc: A clever, omnivorous bird that feeds at carcasses among other foods.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: A flexible predator and scavenger. GloBI records show it eating prairie dogs, pronghorn, deer and elk.

nodes.name: Cougar
nodes.desc: A secretive big cat of the badlands that preys mainly on deer and elk.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: A large raptor that hunts prairie dogs, rabbits and ground squirrels over open ground.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Drives the growth of the prairie grasses and shrubs.

nodes.name: Rain & snow
nodes.desc: Precipitation is scarce in this semi-arid country, and it controls how green the grass gets.

nodes.name: Little Missouri River
nodes.desc: The river that carved the badlands and runs through all three units of the park.

nodes.name: Prairie fire
nodes.desc: Fire is one of the environmental factors the park manages, including prescribed burns that clear old growth.

nodes.name: Badlands soil
nodes.desc: Nutrients in the soil feed the grasses and shrubs.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and insects that break down dead plants and carcasses.
